⚠️ severity: IMPORTANT —
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the abort error directs users to a config key that does not exist**

The terminal text says:

> If this repetition is intentional (a watch or polling command), declare the tool in `agent.identicalCallExemptTools` to opt it out per call site.

`agent.identicalCallExemptTools` is not a real setting: `grep -rn identicalCall lib/src/config lib/src/hosts lib/src/task lib/src/cli bin` returns zero hits — the only opt-out surface is the programmatic `AgentLoopConfig.identicalCallExemptTools` field, which **nothing in the repo passes** (not `_createLoopConfig` in `agent.dart`, not task wiring, not host wiring). A user (or an unattended workflow) who hits the honest abort on a legitimate polling loop has no reachable remedy, in any shipped host — the error text sends them to a dead key.

The sibling breaker set the precedent the text assumes: `agent.misuseBreaker` is a real config key (`config_service.dart:1572`). The ticket AC likewise asks the opt-out to be usable for "intentional polling loops … e.g. watch commands".

Fix (either):
1. Wire the key the text names — `agent.identicalCallExemptTools` in `config_service.dart` (a string-list setting next to `misuseBreaker`) and pass it through `_createLoopConfig`/host wiring; or
2. If no config knob is intended this round, reword the text to the programmatic field (`AgentLoopConfig.identicalCallExemptTools`) and file the config-key follow-up.

Option 1 is preferable: today the CLI's polling users would be aborted at 8 identical calls with no escape hatch at all.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
💡 severity: SUGGESTION —
💡 **SUGGESTION: the constructor's "≤ 0 disables" contract is only enforced by the loop, not the class**

`IdenticalCallLoopGuard`'s doc says "[noticeThreshold] ≤ 0 disables the whole guard", but the class itself only asserts `noticeThreshold != 0` — and asserts are debug-only. In a release build, a directly constructed `IdenticalCallLoopGuard(noticeThreshold: -1)` passes the assert and then fires the notice on the **first** turn of every streak (`_streak >= noticeThreshold` → `1 >= -1`), the exact opposite of the documented disable. The shipped loop is unaffected (`agent_loop.dart:1216` guards with `> 0` before constructing), but the class is exported from the public barrel (`flutter_agent_harness.dart:14`), so SDK consumers can construct it directly.

Compare the abort side, which does handle it defensively (`_streak >= abortThreshold && abortThreshold > 0`).

Fix: `assert(noticeThreshold > 0)` (and mirror the abort-side `> 0` check for the notice arm), so the class honors its own documented ≤ 0 disable semantics regardless of caller.

⚠️ **Fixed — option 1: the key the abort text names now exists, end-to-end.**

`agent.identicalCallExemptTools` is now a real, wired setting (a list of tool-name strings next to `agent.misuseBreaker`, following the gh-1572 wiring precedent):

- **yaml schema** — `lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart`: `_parseAgentSection` accepts `identicalCallExemptTools` (strict: a list of tool-name strings; scalars and non-string entries throw `ConfigException`), stored on `_AgentSection` and `CliConfig` (`final List<String> identicalCallExemptTools`), threaded through `copyWith`, and rendered by the emitter (`_agentSectionYaml`) only when non-empty — the file's defaults-never-written rule.
- **strict mirror** — `lib/src/config/config_service.dart`: `_agentKeyValidators['identicalCallExemptTools']` mirrors the boot parser's rule by value (the file cannot import `cli_config.dart`), so `fa config check` accepts exactly what the boot accepts and the emitter↔validator parity holds.
- **host wiring** — `bin/fah_runapp.dart` (`saved.identicalCallExemptTools.toSet()` → `AgentCliConfig`) → `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart` (`AgentWiringSpec` for the main agent **and** `SubagentServices` for children) → `lib/src/hosts/host_agent_wiring.dart` (`AgentWiringSpec` → `Agent`, and `SubagentServices` → `TaskToolConfig`) → `lib/src/agent/agent.dart` (`_createLoopConfig` passes `identicalCallExemptTools` into every `AgentLoopConfig`).
- **child wiring** — `lib/src/task/task_tool.dart` + `lib/src/task/task_executor.dart`: the set reaches every spawned child at both spawn sites, next to the misuse breaker — a child running a watch command gets the same escape hatch (the issue-#862 precedent).

The abort text at `loop_guard.dart` needed no edit: `agent.identicalCallExemptTools` is now true, and a CLI polling user hitting the 8-call abort has a reachable remedy in the shipped host.

**Tests** (RED-first, all failed against the pre-fix tree at compile/assert stage):
- `test/cli/cli_config_test.dart` — parses the list, defaults to empty when absent, rejects a scalar with the exact message `"agent.identicalCallExemptTools" must be a list of tool names`, rejects a non-string entry.
- `test/config/config_service_test.dart` — mirror-parity test (boot reject ⇔ validator reject ⇔ good parse) plus the new shape in the mechanical emitter↔validator parity list.
- `test/hosts/host_agent_wiring_test.dart` — `identicalCallExemptTools` threads through `AgentWiringSpec` to `Agent` (asserted on `stack.agent`), and the default stays empty.

Fixed in the rework commit on `ai/gh-2461`.

comments.body:
💡 **Fixed — the class now enforces its own documented ≤ 0 disable.**

`lib/src/agent/loop_guard.dart` (`IdenticalCallLoopGuard` constructor + `acceptTurn`), both halves of the suggested fix:

1. The assert is tightened to `assert(noticeThreshold > 0, ...)` — in debug/test builds a non-positive threshold can no longer construct the guard at all.
2. The notice arm mirrors the abort side's defensive check:

```dart
if (_streak >= noticeThreshold &&
    noticeThreshold > 0 &&
    !_noticeDeliveredThisStreak) {
```

so in a **release** build (asserts off) a directly constructed `IdenticalCallLoopGuard(noticeThreshold: -1)` now honors the documented disable — `1 >= -1` can no longer arm the notice on the first turn of every streak. `abortThreshold ≤ 0` keeps its existing "disables only the abort" semantics.

The shipped loop was already null-guarding (`agent_loop.dart` constructs the guard only when `identicalCallNoticeThreshold > 0`), so CLI/SDK behavior through `AgentLoopConfig` is byte-identical; this closes the direct-construction hole the barrel export leaves open.

**Test** (RED-first): `test/agent/loop_guard_test.dart` — "unit: threshold contract": `IdenticalCallLoopGuard(noticeThreshold: 0)` and `(-1)` both throw `AssertionError`. The `-1` case failed against the pre-fix tree (the old `!= 0` assert let it construct and arm). The release-side runtime mirror is exercised by the same construction contract it guards; the loop-level disable stays pinned by the existing "the guard is fully disabled with noticeThreshold 0" test.

Fixed in the rework commit on `ai/gh-2461`.

## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The gh-2461 loop guard is well-built (provider-agnostic streak detection, outcome-aware verdicts, 26 targeted tests pass, format/analyze clean), but two important issues weaken it: the streak resets on machine context notices, not only user/steering input, and the abort error directs users to `agent.identicalCallExemptTools` — a config key that does not exist anywhere in the repo.

**Key Issues**:
- ⚠️ `agent_loop.dart:1262` — reset fires for gh-2423 machine notices merged into `pendingMessages`, not just user/steering input; near-limit notices fire exactly in the incident shape and buy the loop 5 more identical calls per notice.
- ⚠️ `loop_guard.dart:237` — the honest abort names `agent.identicalCallExemptTools`, which no host/CLI/task/config wiring provides; legitimate polling loops have no reachable opt-out in any shipped host.
- 💡 `loop_guard.dart` — constructor lets a negative `noticeThreshold` arm the notice on the first turn; the documented ≤ 0 disable holds only via the loop's own null-guard.

**Digest** (below thread bar, no action required):
- `misuse_breaker.dart:52` — pre-existing: `argsKey` uses order-sensitive `arguments.toString()`; the new guard's canonical JSON is strictly better — worth sharing.
- `agent_loop.dart:1332` — the notice injection block duplicates `_injectPendingMessages`'s body verbatim; the helper call would do.
- Ticket AC note (accepted deviation, documented in the PR): the pre/post-upgrade REG A/B on the recorded session window was not executable (owner-local 6.3 GB assets); constructed replay/projection windows pin the same invariants instead.

**Next Steps**:
1. Reset the streak only on real steering (capture before notices merge into `pendingMessages`) + pin it with a test.
2. Either wire `agent.identicalCallExemptTools` through `config_service`/host wiring or reword the abort text to the programmatic field.
3. Tighten the constructor assert to `noticeThreshold > 0`.

## Automated Code Review — APPROVE (re-review round 2)

**Summary**: All three round-1 findings are fixed in the rework with citable hunks and pin tests; the re-review of the new hunks (+339/−10 across 16 files) surfaced no new issues — 309 targeted tests pass, format and analyzer clean.

**Key Issues**: None open.

- F1 ✅ fixed — `agent_loop.dart:1257-1268`: `steeringArrived` is captured before the gh-2423 machine notices merge into `pendingMessages`, so only real user/steering input resets the streak; pinned by `loop_guard_test.dart` "a queued context notice does NOT reset the streak" (9 reads + mid-streak notice → honest abort at 8).
- F2 ✅ fixed — `agent.identicalCallExemptTools` is now a real, reachable setting end-to-end: strict yaml parser (`cli_config.dart`), by-value validator mirror (`config_service.dart`, `fa config check` parity pinned), emitter, `CliConfig` → `AgentCliConfig` (`fah_runapp.dart:1853`), main agent (`agent_cli.dart:928`) and every spawned child (`SubagentServices`/`task_executor`/`task_tool`/`host_agent_wiring`). The abort text's remedy is now deliverable.
- F3 ✅ fixed — `loop_guard.dart:129`: `assert(noticeThreshold > 0)` plus the release-side runtime mirror in `acceptTurn`; construction-time test pins the contract.

**Next Steps**: Merge. No rework needed; remaining polish is optional and non-blocking.
